issue.title: 关于后续大模型微调部分
issue.body: 您好，想请教一下作者，在使用LETTER得到了物品的token表示组合后，将新的token加入tokenizer后仅使用lora-finetune是否无法学习到新加入token的embedding呢，这样如何保证最后推荐结果是真实的物品token组合呢

comments.body:
Hii 感谢对我们工作的关注。这个问题很重要，所以为了广泛的可读性，我下面用英文回答。

There is one major question summarized from your description:

- Q1: "After adding new tokens to the tokenizer, will using only LoRA fine-tuning fail to learn the embeddings of the newly added tokens?"

- A1: If we simply use LoRA to fine-tune, which means that the parameters being optimized are the QKV matrices of the transformer, the token embeddings will not be updated. However, we can ensure that the token embeddings are trainable by changing p.requires_grad = False to p.requires_grad = True in line 102 of 'LETTER-LC-Rec/lora_finetune.py'.

The results reported in the paper were obtained with `p.requires_grad = False`. Thanks to the improved tokenizer, which combines collaborative signals and code diversity, it indeed achieves better results than LC-Rec even without tuning the corresponding token embeddings. Moreover, I recently found that if we set `p.requires_grad = True`, the performance of both 'LC-Rec' and 'LETTER-LC-Rec' improves, and the latter still maintains a consistent improvement over the former. And this observation aligns well with our expectations.

I plan to revise the reported performance after conducting meticulous experiments. Please stay tuned, and I apologize for any misunderstanding. 

: )

There is one major question summarized from your description:

  • Q1: "After adding new tokens to the tokenizer, will using only LoRA fine-tuning fail to learn the embeddings of the newly added tokens?"

  • A1: If we simply use LoRA to fine-tune, which means that the parameters being optimized are the QKV matrices of the transformer, the token embeddings will not be updated. However, we can ensure that the token embeddings are trainable by changing p.requires_grad = False to p.requires_grad = True in line 102 of 'LETTER-LC-Rec/lora_finetune.py'.

The results reported in the paper were obtained with p.requires_grad = False. Thanks to the improved tokenizer, which combines collaborative signals and code diversity, it indeed achieves better results than LC-Rec even without tuning the corresponding token embeddings. Moreover, I recently found that if we set p.requires_grad = True, the performance of both 'LC-Rec' and 'LETTER-LC-Rec' improves, and the latter still maintains a consistent improvement over the former. And this observation aligns well with our expectations.

I plan to revise the reported performance after conducting meticulous experiments. Please stay tuned, and I apologize for any misunderstanding.
